clue.text: What makes you think home support should go first?

indicators.note: going first means being placed at the front, so the second item named is written before the first

blocks.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: Someone muses on whether backing at home ought to come before everything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home support' reads as one idea, but it is two pieces: home and support, with support placed in front.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ inside your skull does the thinking, so a descriptive phrase for it works as the definition.

clue.text: Where a Soviet hammer is delivered in vehicle

indicators.note: a speech or line is delivered by voice, so we want how the phrase is spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: on the Soviet flag the hammer sits beside the sickle

explanation.surface: A sentence about where some Soviet hammer is handed over inside a van or truck.
explanation.walkthrough: The Soviet emblem is the hammer and sickle, so the hammer is 'by sickle', which said out loud is BICYCLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedal-powered two-wheeler is a means of transport, so it counts as a vehicle.

clue.text: Tuna, roast nuts and rocket filling?

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters before it are scrambled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A list of sandwich fillings: tuna, roast nuts, and rocket, the salad leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: Rocket looks like the salad leaf in a sandwich, and nuts like another filling; in fact nuts is the signal and rocket is the spacecraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew member travelling inside a spacecraft is what fills the rocket, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Northern people carrying duck back to their county

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so only that letter is kept
in a down entry the lower piece carries the ones on top of it, so it is written after them

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for northern
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, shaped like zero
the final letter
folk are people

explanation.surface: People from the north take a duck home with them to the shire they come from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck back' looks like a unit, a reversal of some duck, but back attaches to the next word. Norfolk is an English county on the east coast, its name meaning 'north folk'.
explanation.definitionFit: Norfolk is one of the counties of England, an example of the category.

clue.text: Timidity of fighting fish going around cold water

indicators.note: to go around something is to encircle it, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: a cod is a sea fish
war is fighting
ice is frozen, cold water

explanation.surface: A fighting fish that shies away from cold water shows a lack of nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fighting fish' suggests the Siamese fighting fish, but fighting and fish are separate pieces, the second wrapped round the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Timidity and the answer both name a lack of courage, so they are near synonyms.

clue.text: Dog — setter? — under my girlfriend’s top

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter in a down clue, so only the opening letter is kept
in a down entry, being under something means being written after it

blocks.note: Cor! and My! are both exclamations of surprise
the opening letter of the word
the setter refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: A dog, possibly a setter, curled up beneath a girlfriend's top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter?' teases the dog breed but means the puzzle's setter, I; 'my' is the exclamation Cor, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: The corgi is a short-legged Welsh herding breed, so it is an example of a dog.

clue.text: Brill, with flounder, swimming

indicators.note: something swimming moves about freely, so the letters are moved into a new order

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
taken as written

explanation.surface: A brill, a flatfish, is out swimming alongside a flounder, another flatfish.
explanation.walkthrough: Brill and flounder are both flatfish, so Brill looks like a fish; here it is the British slang word, short for brilliant.
explanation.definitionFit: Brill is informal British slang meaning excellent or great, a close synonym.

clue.text: Foreigners abandoned by street’s side

indicators.note: to be abandoned by something is to lose its company, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: strangers are people from elsewhere
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Outsiders are left behind on the side of the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Street's side' reads as the edge of a road; side is actually the definition, a sports team.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangers is a Glasgow football club, and a side is a sports team, so it is an example.

clue.text: Start to drink unwrapped bubbly

indicators.note: unwrapping takes off the outer covering, so the first and last letters go
bubbly means fizzing and lively, so the letters jostle into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the word without its outer letters

explanation.surface: An invitation to open a bottle of champagne and get drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: Bubbly wants to be champagne, the thing drunk; it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is an informal short form of introduction, the opening part of something.

clue.text: Clear old cupboard

blocks.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a press is an old word, still used in Ireland and Scotland, for a cupboard

explanation.surface: An instruction to empty out an antique cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: Clear looks like a verb, to empty; it is the adjective, as in an express wish. A press is a cupboard for linen or clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Express as an adjective means explicitly stated, so an express instruction is a plain, unambiguous one.

clue.text: One serving three queens

blocks.note: a queen is a female cat
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the cipher of Queen Elizabeth
the same royal cipher a second time

explanation.surface: A footman or attendant waiting on three royal ladies at once.
explanation.walkthrough: Three queens are three different pieces: a queen cat, then two of the royal monogram.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm or person supplying and serving food at functions is someone who serves.

clue.text: Restless navy on vessels heading west

indicators.note: in an across answer west is leftward, so travelling west means reading right to left

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for navy
taken as written
pots are vessels for cooking or holding things

explanation.surface: A fleet of ships sailing westward without pause.
explanation.walkthrough: The navy and vessels suggest ships, but the vessels are kitchen pots, and only they turn round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something non-stop never pauses or rests, so it is continuous and without respite.

clue.text: Thick-skinned swimmer going back in Hathersage Lido — ‘Cor! Chilly!’

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the phrase that follows, running across its word breaks
going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the letters read right to left

blocks.note: the run of letters from the end of the town name to the start of the last word

explanation.surface: A hardy outdoor swimmer at a Derbyshire open-air pool complains about the cold water.
explanation.walkthrough: Hathersage Lido is an outdoor pool in the Peak District; the thick-skinned swimmer sounds like a hardy bather, but it is a reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: The reptile has armoured, leathery hide and spends much time in water, so it is literally thick-skinned and a swimmer.

clue.text: In secret, go and spin disc by the Electric Light Orchestra

indicators.note: to spin is to turn round, so the letters are turned to face the other way

blocks.note: ELO is the band's usual initials
an EP, extended play, is a type of record

explanation.surface: Secretly heading off to play a record by the 1970s rock band ELO.
explanation.walkthrough: In secret, go is the definition, run away to marry; 'by' places one piece beside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Couples who run off secretly to marry without consent are said to do this, so it means a clandestine departure.

clue.text: Time of The Rapture

indicators.note: made of means drawn from, so the letters are taken from within the words that follow

blocks.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: The religious end times when believers are taken up to heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make The Rapture look like a title or the religious event; the letters run across its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a period of history, and time is used the same way, as in 'in Victorian times'.

clue.text: Say, Henry V, Carrie, Us, Face Off and The Birds

indicators.note: with its face off a word has lost its front, so its first letter is removed

blocks.note: Henry V was an English monarch, an example of one
Carrie Fisher, the actress who played Princess Leia
taken as written

explanation.surface: A list of film titles: Henry V, Carrie, Us, Face/Off and Hitchcock's The Birds.
explanation.walkthrough: Every item looks like a film; only The Birds really is one in this reading, as the definition. Face Off works on the title before it.
explanation.definitionFit: These small, brightly coloured diving birds are an example of birds, so a plural name fits the plural definition.

clue.text: Huge robin disturbed one with adjoining garden?

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A giant robin is upset by the person whose garden backs onto ours.
explanation.walkthrough: The robin is a common garden bird in Britain, so the scene of a disturbed bird and the next-door garden fits together.
explanation.definitionFit: The person living next door typically has a garden bordering yours, a descriptive definition marked by the question mark.

clue.text: One wearing medal with a YES pasted on is happy doing anything

indicators.note: to be pasted is to be thrashed, so the letters are knocked into a new order
something worn is put on and enclosed by the wearer, so one piece goes inside another
in a down entry, being on something means sitting above it, so it is written first

blocks.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
gong is British slang for a medal or honour

explanation.surface: Someone with a medal and a 'YES' sticker on them is content with any plan.
explanation.walkthrough: The medal wears the one, so the numeral goes inside it. Pasted means beaten up, not stuck on.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy-going person is relaxed and tolerant, so they are content to go along with whatever is suggested.

clue.text: Boisterous woman beginning to lose it with her boring relative

indicators.note: boisterous means rowdy and unruly, so the letters are jumbled
the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept
to bore is to drill into something, so one piece is pushed inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rowdy woman starts losing her temper at her tedious relation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lose it' reads as losing one's temper; only the first letter of lose is used, and it stands alone. Boring means drilling, not dull.
explanation.definitionFit: A spouse's mother is a relation by marriage, so she is a kind of relative.

clue.text: Representation of Solomon cuddling Solomon’s little sibling

indicators.note: to cuddle is to wrap your arms round someone, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: the setter, Solomon, refers to himself as me
read as 'Solomon is', which the setter would say as I'm
sis is the short form of sister

explanation.surface: A portrait shows Solomon hugging his small brother or sister.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s looks possessive but is 'is', and the setter's name stands for the first person each time.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimesis is the imitation or portrayal of the real world in art, so it is a form of representation.

clue.text: Obscure videos screened by tech company

indicators.note: something screened is hidden behind a barrier, so one piece is shut inside another

blocks.note: clips are short videos
EE is a British mobile phone and broadband company

explanation.surface: Little-known videos are being shown by a technology firm.
explanation.walkthrough: Obscure looks like an adjective, little-known, and screened like broadcast; both are deceptions, the definition being the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse something is to block it from view or overshadow it, which matches the verb sense of obscure.

clue.text: Say “cut” before Disney film’s ended

indicators.note: coming before means placed in front, so the first item is written first

blocks.note: a cut is one kind of injury
Up is a 2009 Disney-Pixar animated film

explanation.surface: A director calls 'cut' before a Disney movie has finished shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' in quotes sounds like a director's call; 'say' marks it as an example of an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind up a meeting or business is to bring it to a close, so the past tense matches ended.

clue.text: Spouse regularly rejected request for help

indicators.note: at regular intervals means every other letter, so alternate ones are kept
something rejected is sent back, so the letters are read in the other direction

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A husband or wife who keeps being turned down calls out for assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters read the same both ways, so turning them back changes nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Morse distress signal is the international call for rescue, so it is a plea for assistance.

clue.text: Child suppresses desire to become theatre worker

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold something down and keep it in, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: a son is a child
an urge is a desire

explanation.surface: A child hides their dream of a career on the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Theatre suggests acting, but it is the operating theatre of a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons work in an operating theatre, so the crossword-style description fits this medical profession.

clue.text: Heads of Müller and Onken lug about big cheese

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letters are kept

blocks.note: the opening letter
the opening letter
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: Müller and Onken are yoghurt brands sold in Britain, which makes big cheese look like dairy produce rather than the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A big cheese is slang for an important, powerful person, and a mogul is a powerful business magnate.

clue.text: Tips from gourmand — use allotment-grown vegetables and fruit

blocks.note: the opening letter
the opening letter
the opening letter
the opening letter
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A food lover's advice: cook with vegetables grown on your own allotment.
explanation.walkthrough: Tips reads as advice from the gourmand, but it means the word ends. An allotment is a rented plot for growing vegetables in Britain.

clue.text: Meat flipped on bread?

blocks.note: surface reading: some meat tossed onto a slice of bread
setter's reading: a patty turned on the griddle and served in a bun

explanation.walkthrough: Flipped looks like a reversal signal, but it is literal: the patty is flipped while it cooks, and then it goes in a bun.
explanation.definitionFit: A grilled minced-beef patty served in a bread roll is exactly this fast-food item.

clue.text: Moan oddly and cry like a crow or parrot

blocks.note: the first and third letters
a caw is the harsh call of a crow

explanation.walkthrough: Crow or parrot reads as a pair of birds to imitate; the crow belongs to the wordplay and only the parrot is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The macaw is a large, brightly coloured South American bird of the parrot family.

clue.text: Business behind counterfeit beauty product

indicators.note: being behind something means coming after it, so this piece follows the other

clue.text: Laws broken by one in Bremen getting pills?

explanation.definitionFit: Codeine is an opioid painkiller usually taken as tablets, so it can be described loosely by its form.

clue.text: External body assembled to reduce murder rates

definitions.text: External body assembled to reduce murder rates

blocks.clueFragment: External body assembled to reduce murder rates
blocks.note: surface reading: an outside agency set up to bring down the homicide figures
setter's reading: a murder is the collective noun for crows, and a stuffed figure outdoors scares them away

explanation.walkthrough: External body sounds like an outside inquiry; it is a figure of a body, stuffed and assembled, standing out in a field.

clue.text: One by Spring’s end getting into nature-god?

definitions.text: One by Spring’s end getting into nature-god?

indicators.note: an end of a word is its final letter, so only that letter is used

blocks.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: A worshipper drawn in by Pan at the end of spring.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: one who has got into a nature-god, keen on the season's rites, is a heathen.
